title: Interlude: The Mysterious Future Baron【Alicia Gran Oldwood】
content: From the moment I became aware of my surroundings, I, Alicia Gran Oldwood, already had my marriage partner decided for me.
His name was Edward Gran Aetherdam, the crown prince of the Aetherdam Kingdom.
I would never forget the day I first met him, accompanied by my parents.
With beautiful golden hair like the sun and eyes that sparkled like shining stars, his somewhat ephemeral expression was more than enough to captivate a young girl at first glance.
Ah, I was born for this person, I thought.
His Highness was first in line for the throne, and it was already decided that I, his fiancée, would become queen in the future.
Aetherdam was a proud nation that valued magical traditions, and I never found it boring to walk along the predetermined path laid out for me.
Rather, the path stretching out before me was more glorious than that of other nobles, with a prestigious position beside His Highness at the end.
So, I worked hard.
I aimed to become a worthy presence beside His Highness, dedicating my studies in magic and everything else for him, and for my parents who arranged our engagement.
However, I made a significant blunder.
Unable to keep His Highness's heart tethered to me, I challenged a commoner woman to a duel out of childish jealousy, only to suffer a foolish defeat in front of the public.
Having lived my life for His Highness, it was undeniable that I felt an indescribable anxiety and disgust at the sight of an unknown woman standing where I was supposed to be, next to him.
If only I could have held back, but the entourage, who found the situation of a commoner attending a noble academy amusing, reacted excessively, and I couldn't suppress it.

On the stage of the duel that had formed without my knowledge, no matter how I tried to maneuver, it only led to digging my own grave, resulting in ugly injuries that rendered me useless as a noble daughter.
I resented the entourage that had run wild without my knowledge, but it was also a result of my own inability to control the situation.
When His Highness announced the annulment of our engagement, I received words like these:
"I don't like traditions or customs; I don't like the predetermined path."
"Do you know my favorite food? My favorite place, my favorite book, my favorite games? You wouldn't know, would you..."
"You are the model of a noble. I couldn't bring myself to like you, who lived according to your parents' words; it was painful."
"Patricia gently embraced my feelings. She took me around the stalls in the town and made heartfelt dishes and sweets for me."
Indeed, it was just as His Highness said.
I knew he often sneaked into the town out of curiosity, but I had never been interested in what he did.
I had no interest in the adventurous tales he liked, nor in the mischievous games, and I couldn't cook or make sweets.
I thought the servants would handle all those things, and I never doubted that was what being a noble meant.
I truly believed that my duty was to become a talented woman who would not be ashamed to stand beside His Highness when I became queen...
After my defeat, I was painfully made aware that I no longer existed in His Highness's heart, and I accepted the situation of being married off to the Discarded Land with my parents' scolding.
What is love? What is affection? — It's complicated and elusive.
The feelings and efforts I had spent over the past several years were undeniable facts, but the blind faith I had in them meant nothing to His Highness.
Having lost everything, I no longer understood anything.
The Brave family's mansion was completely devoid of any decorative furnishings, and the only sounds that occasionally broke the silence were the voices and footsteps of the servants.

I found it a bit strange that the dark emotions that had been trying to fill my heart since I arrived at this house were settling down, and unlike when I lived in the royal capital, I wasn't plagued by nightmares.
Having come to this distant land known as the Discarded Land, perhaps I had reached a state of resignation, believing I would never return to the duke's house again.
The simple room, the simple clothes, the simple meals—everything I had lost felt just right for me now.
For five days, I had done nothing but sit quietly in my room, giving me plenty of time to think, yet I spent my time in a void, not knowing what to do next.
At that moment, there was a knock on the door in the morning.
"Alicia-sama, good morning! It's breakfast."
The voice belonged to the young future Baron, who was the same age as me.
It was the first time I had heard his voice since we first met.
It was a bit painful to be met with that carefree smile now, and more than anything, I felt a sense of confusion, so I didn't want to see him.
Knock knock knock! Crack crack crack!
As I remained silent, the knocking grew stronger, as if the door would break.
"I'm awake! I'm awake, so come in! The door will break!"
When I finally raised my voice after a long time, he entered with a casual "Excuse me."
When I asked him what he would do if the door broke, he replied with a carefree smile, "We can just fix it again."
I truly couldn't comprehend it.
As I was feeling exasperated, he took out a coffee set from the wagon and began pouring the black liquid into a cup.
"Do you want milk? How about sugar?"
When he asked me, I couldn't respond.
I had never drunk coffee before.
"I... I don't know because I've never had it. At home, tea was the norm."
When I answered honestly, he looked a bit apologetic as he said,
"I'm sorry we couldn't prepare tea; after all, it's a rural territory in the frontier."
"...I don't mind."
This was not the duke's house but the Brave family.
My place now was this simple room, so coffee was more than enough.
Thinking that, I took a big sip, only to cough at the overwhelming bitterness.
"Cough cough, it's... bitter..."
"You drank it black right away. Let's start with something sweet."
The coffee he handed me instead was mixed with milk and sugar, and it had a sweet, gentle taste.
This was drinkable and not bad; in fact, it felt warmer to my heart than the tea I had been drinking out of concern for appearances.
"I was curious about something," I said, feeling a little more relaxed.
"Why are you personally serving me when there are servants?"
Until now, the servants had quietly delivered my meals, but today was different, so I asked without thinking.
"Simply because we're short-handed. If needed, the servants will fight, and just the other day, most of them died in battle."
"...I see."
The answer to my casual question was heavier than I had expected.
A mysterious man who doesn't quite fit, just like when I first met him.
Not knowing how to respond, I fell silent, and Lagna suddenly lifted my bangs.
"Alicia-sama, you are a remarkable person."
As I tried to turn my face away, he grabbed my chin, preventing me from moving.
What on earth is this man!
Ignoring the glare I shot at him, Lagna continued speaking.
"Here, it's a testament to the pride you fought with and a symbol of courage. Of course, I have my own as well."
As he said this, he pushed his bangs aside, revealing painful scars that looked like they had been stitched multiple times on his forehead.
Upon closer inspection, I could see several scars on his neck, hidden by his clothing.
In a place known as the Discarded Land, which often faced skirmishes with neighboring countries and monster attacks, it seemed to be a testament to those who had survived.
"In our family, we don't deny scars. Rather, we take pride in them."

He spoke similar words to those of a lower noble who had approached me after the duel incident, saying, "Even if you're damaged, your beauty remains unchanged," but his words carried a different weight.
I stopped glaring and chewed on his words.
A testament to having fought, huh... Was it really something that could be called a fight...?
What was I even trying to fight for? Ah, I don't know.
"Haha, well, the reason I brought breakfast was also to talk with you."
In front of my silence, Lagna suddenly released my chin and took a step back, awkwardly smiling as he changed the subject.
"It's a rough territory with nothing, but the nature is rich, so why not take a walk together? In the face of nature, human conflicts are trivial here."
"Trivial..."
Was my reason for fighting noble pride? The responsibilities of the duke's house?
No, it wasn't anything so grand.
I simply couldn't accept that another woman was in my place, and I overreacted, ending up in a situation from which I could never return.
Trivial, there must have been so many other things I could have done, yet here I was, feeling so small.
As my feelings began to sink deeper, my fiancé Lagna kindly invited me, so I responded.
"...I'll go."
It would be bothersome to spend my time gloomily in someone else's house, and it was important to breathe in some fresh air.
"Could you please show me around this land?"
"Of course, I'd be happy to."
Despite still being rude, I found myself slightly interested in Lagna, who was trying his best to be considerate, albeit awkwardly.
It felt like a long time since I had directed such a carefree smile at anyone, especially not at His Highness.
After being led outside my room, I got into the prepared carriage, thinking I would be shown around the town, but for some reason, I found myself in the midst of a towering mountain.
"This is the Yudaina Mountain Range, which is beyond human control," Lagna explained, spreading his arms as I grew tired from walking.
I could barely keep up with him as he advanced along the unpaved beast path.
I wiped the sweat dripping down my forehead.
Even though I had worn clothes that allowed for easy movement, the sweat clung to my body, making me feel uncomfortable, but it was still much better than when I was in the royal capital.
"I thought we were going to walk in the town, not in the mountains... I expected to be introduced to shops or local specialties made from nature..."
As I tried to catch my breath and said this, he laughed and replied,
"Haha, there's nothing like that."
What was with that smile? It was a bit infuriating.
"If we decorate the territory poorly, the rough crowd won't accept it, and if the enemy finds it attractive, the damage will increase."
As he said, there was nothing glamorous in the town I saw from the carriage window.
The town was as simple as the Brave family's mansion.
I distinctly remember being shocked by how the entire town seemed built to be destroyed at any moment.
Moreover, I frequently saw residents with injuries, some missing fingers, arms, or even legs, and I felt the weight of my own scars...
This was the Discarded Land.
Yet, people lived here, and children played with carefree smiles, perhaps dreaming of becoming adventurers, seen wielding sticks in play.
For someone like me, who had been born and raised in the royal capital, only knowing the beautiful tourist spots meant for nobles, this was truly another world.
"The only entertainment here is betting on who will die next; it's quite popular."
"R-Really..."
"I heard someone made a profit betting on my dad dying in battle a month ago."
It seemed like a ridiculous bet, but is that what happens when people have no entertainment?
I had been told that Lagna's father and brothers had died in battle last month.
In such a situation, he was genuinely kind to be smiling and keeping me company.
"That's not a conversation for women; I apologize."
"N-No, it's fine. If that's normal here..."
I accepted it as just how things were.
Even if I were scolded and abandoned, I wouldn't be able to smile if my parents died.
"I don't think it's good to get too accustomed to what's normal here."
"Wha—! I'm trying to accept it!"
"It's not that easy to accept."
"What are you talking about?"
I leaned against a nearby tree.
Upon reflection, perhaps trying to accept it was my ego.
Would it be disrespectful to the people living in the Brave Territory?
"I'm not accustomed to it either; if I did, I'd die."
As I took a breath, Lagna said,
"But it's important to know deeply."
"To know deeply..."
Amidst his poor jokes and outrageous rudeness, he occasionally threw words at me that seemed to see right through me.
He seemed to know about the shameful parts I hadn't even spoken of, parts I didn't want to talk about, my irretrievable blunders.
"Both enemies and allies live on the same land, so don't underestimate or overestimate either; know them deeply and prepare—if you want to survive."
Even if this land is hard to accept, knowing it deeply might make it a bit better, he added later.
His words seemed to speak of something entirely different, yet they pierced my heart deeply, resonating with my blunders.
"Everyone fights knowing this land. It's all up to you."
"Right... I had seen the faces of the people living here, but this isn't the place I had heard about."
"The people of the Brave Territory won't laugh at your decisions made after much deliberation."
Then it would be natural for me to be laughed at.
After all, I hadn't even made my own decisions...
"Well, it seems we've gotten a bit gloomy again, huh? You can laugh it off. This is a place where life and death are just stories."
When I fell silent, he scratched his head and laughed.

His demeanor seemed age-appropriate yet gave a somewhat unreliable impression, but when he lined up his words with insight, he appeared more mature than any noble I had met at the academy, even more so than His Highness.
"You're telling me to laugh, then not to laugh; it's confusing."
"Maybe it just means I'm living in the moment? Haha."
What a mismatched and mysterious man.
Then, while he kept saying, "We're almost there," I was led to climb a cliff.
As I huffed and puffed, he offered unnecessary encouragement, saying, "You're just not used to climbing cliffs."
But I didn't want to get used to it.
When I found myself hanging in mid-air, holding onto the cliff with his hand, I firmly resolved not to trust this man and lightly resented him. But—
"Whoa..."
When I finally reached the top of the cliff and saw the view, all my trivial complaints were blown away.
"This is my favorite spot."
He had said a lot of other things, but I couldn't hear any of it; the Discarded Land, no, the Brave Territory was vast.
Truly, truly, everything I had been troubled by, everything I had lost, felt like mere nonsense that had occurred in the small garden of the royal capital.
"Trivial... huh."
As I muttered, Lagna began to ramble about something unrelated, but I told him that wasn't what I meant.
His sulking expression was somewhat amusing.
Having been taken to a dangerous mountain and left hanging on a cliff, I felt a sense of satisfaction in being able to repay him.
All the faction disputes at the academy, the annulment of my engagement—before this overwhelming emotion, everything seemed trivial, yet I held back.
The memories of growing up in the duke's house and my feelings for His Highness were undeniably real, and it felt wrong to forget them as if they were trivial.
Even now, I was filled with uncertainties about what I should have done and what I should do moving forward, but if it were him standing beside me... I decided to ask.
"Lagna-sama, I want to ask you something."
"You can drop the honorifics. I'm not used to being called that."
...This man really can't read the room, can he?
I thought to suggest we drop the formalities, then asked again.
"Hey Lagna. After making a decision after much deliberation, and trying to accept the results, what would you do if you still felt an overwhelming sense of regret?"
"Is the answer that time will heal... just a pretty saying?"
As if he understood himself, Lagna read my expression and answered seriously.
"It's natural that once you make a decision, you can't choose the other option. Even if you clear your resentment, it won't come back."
His answer felt like he could see through my true feelings. He probably knew.
It was true that my engagement had been annulled, but he understood the full scope of it.
"...It's a story from a little while ago."
As I waited for what he would say, he murmured.
He had been betting on his father's death, saying people die easily in this land, and now he spoke seriously about the situation of his family dying in battle.
He had chased down and killed the enemy soldiers who had slain his father.
Dying in battle seemed to be an honor in the Brave Territory.
So, he had been taught repeatedly not to fight with personal grudges, but he couldn't stop himself.
Even in a situation where his trusted father was at a disadvantage, no matter how many sacrifices were made, he had avenged his family who had been killed.
He self-deprecatingly admitted that the current situation of the Brave family being short-handed was a result of such forced actions.
"—No matter how normal it seems, you will regret it. But at that moment, I realized something. It meant that I was loved enough to feel that way, and that there are still people left."
As he gazed down at the Brave Territory, he continued speaking.
"I haven't lost everything; there are still many things left. That's why I want to try hard to be a noble I don't want to be, and I want to go to an academy I don't want to attend."
There are still many things left, huh.
Listening seriously to his words, I pondered whether there was anything left for me, but nothing remained as it always had.
It was only natural; what I had been looking at was not His Highness himself, but only my own figure standing beside the future king.
"...What if there was nothing left? I've been taught since birth what I should do, and I've lived solely for that, but what if it was something I could never achieve again?"
"If you're not dead, there's still something left."
"There's nothing left!"
I raised my voice involuntarily.
"The past me is dead... as the daughter of the duke... that's why I'm in this Discarded Land... Ah, I'm sorry, that was a slip of the tongue."
I had learned from experience that acting on impulse would only lead to failure, yet here I was, acting like a child again.
The burn scar on my left eye throbbed, and my heart began to ache.
As long as this unhealable scar remained, no matter how hard I tried to forget, I could never truly forget.
It felt as if there was an endless swamp at my feet, and the more I struggled, the deeper I sank into the dark depths.
Like Lagna's words, even if I fulfilled my revenge, it would surely be someone else standing beside him, never to be filled again.
...Wouldn't it be easier to just throw myself off this cliff?
This beautiful scenery that made me feel small for worrying about trivial things would become nothing more than a mere landscape if my vision became clouded and I couldn't see anything.
Just as my vision blurred, and I felt my strength leaving me, on the verge of falling—
"Alicia, I will protect you from now on."
Suddenly, those words reached my ears, and my hazy vision sharpened, reflecting Lagna standing there with a serious expression.
What did he just say?
If I didn't mishear him, he said he would protect me from now on?
As I was bewildered, he continued speaking.
"If the daughter of the duke is dead, then the Alicia standing before me now is the one who married into the Brave family."
He then extended his pinky.
"Then I can promise you this: I will definitely protect you."
His answer to my question didn't quite fit, but if I were asked whether I could respond adequately, it would be very difficult, and I would probably only say something as trivial as "time will heal."
After thinking deeply and deeply about the difficult question, his answer was a pinky swear of protection.
"I've been thinking since this morning, but you really have a lot of unexpected words and actions."
When I said this, he scratched his head, looking a bit embarrassed.
"Well, I tried to find something clever to say, but the boys of the Brave family aren't used to this kind of situation, so only my honest words came out."
"...Hehe."
I couldn't help but smile a little at that.
His carefree smile and straightforward words seemed to reflect the way of life in the Brave Territory, living proudly in the moment.
There was no trace of the hypocrisy and deceit characteristic of noble society.
Standing before me as he was, without pretense, made me feel a sense of nostalgia for things I had long forgotten.
"Was it really that strange? I've never said such a line before; my father and brothers were the type to speak through their actions..."
I told Lagna, who was flustered.
"Actually, this is the first time someone has said something like that to my face."
It was said with a direct gaze that pierced my core.
"What? I thought as a duchess, you would have heard it from various people."
"Those who say such unexpected things are often avoided, you know?"
"Damn... All the good lines I secretly practiced for going to the academy are now wasted..."
"What kind of ridiculous practice is that?"
Practicing pick-up lines while walking a blood-soaked life in a war-torn world seemed more likely to make me feel exasperated than to laugh.
What a truly mysterious person.
"But I don't dislike it. It's straightforward."
Perhaps, if I were my younger self, I would have thought it was lame.
Having lived through noble society, experienced failures, and repeatedly questioned myself with His Highness's words in my heart, now, straightforward words reached me deeply.
High-ranking nobles are seen more for their status than as individuals.
His Highness must have been the same.
In a noble society that values tradition, being unable to be seen or understood was exhausting.
Now I understood; it was only natural that I was annulled.
"Indeed, you might be right. I may have been overthinking things."
As I turned my gaze to the scenery, I saw the horizon stretching endlessly.
"Trivial, trivial indeed. Clinging to the past that has vanished, lingering endlessly..."
"Well, that's just how humans are."
"But in the Brave family, isn't that forbidden?"
"Yeah, it's understandable the first time. But from then on, it's important to switch gears."
The past me was dead, and now I was Alicia of the Brave family...
It felt as if the gaping hole in my heart was being filled.
Being here was not a punishment.
I would switch my mindset to see it as a new beginning; that's how it was in the Brave family.

"When I return to the academy with you, you'll probably attract a lot of attention. Honestly, I doubt there will be a place for you, and I think there will be a lot of hostility and malice... but will you still protect me?"
As I said this, I extended my pinky to Lagna, and he tightly linked his with mine.
"I'm good at that kind of thing, so leave it to me."
To an outsider, it might seem like a romantic exchange reminiscent of the stories of heroes and princesses I read as a child, but the scars on our faces made it a bit amusing.
A daughter of a noble who had her engagement annulled and a baron living in the Discarded Land.
As characters in a story, there was a vast difference between us, yet it felt fitting and comfortable for me now.
"Alicia, wait a moment; I want to redo that vow."
I felt suddenly pulled back to reality.
No, I had sensed that he was a rude man devoid of any romantic notions. I tried to calm myself down.
I shouldn't expect such things from Lagna.
"Just wait a moment; I'll call him right now—Onyx!"
The moment Lagna shouted, a massive black dragon descended before us from the sky.

I had never seen one, so I couldn't be sure if it was truly a dragon, but its appearance resembled those depicted in the picture books I had seen as a child, and instinctively, my mind recognized it as a dragon.
Moreover, a black dragon.
In the stories of heroes and princesses, black dragons were often depicted as evil beings, and now, it was glaring at me with its large face.
The moment our eyes met, I lost consciousness in an instant.
This was the encounter between Lagna and me.
Not a hint of romance, but... that was just right.
